questions.prompt: How do you fetch data for a page in the App Router?

options.text: Make the page an async Server Component and await fetch() directly
Fetch in a useEffect in the page component

questions.explanation: Server Components can be async and await data inline. getServerSideProps and useEffect are not needed for reads in the App Router.

questions.prompt: Two independent fetches don't depend on each other. What's the best way to load them?

options.text: await one, then await the other

questions.explanation: Independent requests should run in parallel via Promise.all to avoid a waterfall where each waits for the previous.

questions.prompt: Next.js automatically de-duplicates identical fetch() calls in a single render. What is this feature called (two words)?
questions.explanation: Request memoization dedupes identical fetch() calls made during one render pass into a single request.

questions.prompt: Which are true about fetching in Server Components? Select all that apply.

options.text: You can query a database or ORM directly
Secrets and API keys stay on the server
The data ends up in the initial HTML
You must expose a public API for the browser to call

questions.explanation: Server Components can query databases directly, keep secrets server-side, and render data into the HTML — no public API required.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of rendering a data-driven Server Component page.

items.text: The async page component runs on the server
It awaits the data it needs (in parallel where possible)
It renders to HTML with the data included
The HTML is sent to the browser

questions.explanation: The server runs the async component, awaits data, renders HTML containing that data, and sends it to the browser.

questions.prompt: Match each data-fetching concept to its meaning.

pairs.left: await fetch in a Server Component
pairs.right: Read data on the server before rendering
De-duplicate identical fetch calls in one render
Slow sequential awaits that don't need to be

questions.explanation: Server-side await reads data before render, Promise.all parallelizes independent requests, memoization dedupes identical fetches, and a waterfall is avoidable sequential awaiting.
